title: Latino-Owned Coffee Shop Closes After Claims That Founder Works for ICE
description: Tasa Coffee Roasters in Chicago permanently closed its doors after workers walked out in protest.
author: Madaleine Rubin and Madison Malone Kircher

title: Abrego Garcia Will Voluntarily Leave U.S., Ending 20-Month Legal Ordeal
description: Kilmar Armando Abrego Garcia, who was wrongfully deported last year, is leaving for Spain. He had faced the prospect that the Trump administration might deport him to Liberia.
author: Alan Feuer

title: Sullivan Concedes Alaska Senate Race to Peltola
description: The Republican conceded five days after the Trump administration gave up on a long-shot lawsuit intended to potentially block certification of the race.
author: Tim Balk

title: Prosecutor Urged Justice Dept. to Reconsider Charges Against Fugitive, Email Shows
description: Aaron Reitz, the U.S. attorney in Houston, questioned the indictment of a Chicago doctor who fled the country after being accused of defrauding taxpayers. The man later donated to Mr. Reitz’s campaign.
author: Glenn Thrush

title: An Explosion Is Coming to Iowa. And Residents Can’t Do a Thing About It.
description: Residents of Middletown, which adjoins an Army facility where dangerous chemicals will be detonated Wednesday, are taping up their doors and getting ready to flee.
author: Maia Spoto and Jack Healy

title: Blanche Downplays Questions Over Nvidia as Investigators Examine Company’s Customers
description: Justice Department investigators have gathered evidence of Nvidia’s high-powered computer chips being illegally diverted by other firms to China, according to people familiar with the inquiries.
author: Devlin Barrett and Ana Swanson

title: MAGA Attacked Harvard. So Harvard Taught a Class About It.
description: The Make America Great Again movement wants to remake Harvard. Harvard has a class for that.
author: Mark Arsenault

title: U.S. Spy Agencies Suffer Breach of Some Unclassified Information
description: The intrusion affecting the C.I.A. and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence comes amid heightened concerns about cybersecurity.
author: Dustin Volz, Tyler Pager and Julian E. Barnes

title: Officials Dismiss Rental Car Felony Charge for Incoming House Democrat
description: Representative-elect LaKesha Womack in North Carolina had been issued a criminal summons at a campaign rally last month about a rental vehicle she had failed to return in 2019.
author: Eduardo Medina

title: Trump Awards Rudy Giuliani Presidential Medal of Freedom
description: The award honored a Trump ally who was once known as “America’s mayor” but whose reputation was tarnished by his efforts to overturn the 2020 election on behalf of the president.
author: Erica L. Green

title: Unstoppable Crowds Are Meeting Up to Push Immovable Objects
description: In Chicago, St. Louis, New York and Washington dreamers and pranksters have gotten together recently aiming to shift massive landmarks.
author: Victor Mather

title: Trump Ballroom and Other Projects Got $300 Million Donation Boost
description: The Trump administration declined to say who donated those funds to an account funding presidential projects like the White House ballroom and the triumphal arch.
author: David A. Fahrenthold, Zachary Small and Luke Broadwater

title: Broderick Wins Tennessee House Race, Giving Democrats Largest Majority in 30 Years
description: Democrats’ midterm rout kept expanding in the House after a tech support worker ousted an eight-term Republican without having aired a single TV ad.
author: John Yoon and Emily Cochrane

title: Why Chicago’s Tax Incentive Program Fell Short in Low-Income Neighborhoods
description: An examination by The Times shows how a tax incentive program that transformed downtown has left some poorer neighborhoods overlooked and neglected.
author: Nell Salzman and Joshua Lott

title: How a Scientist Behind the Mediterranean Diet Got Caught in Trump’s War on Harvard
description: Walter Willett studies the link between diet and health, a high priority for Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. His grants were frozen anyway.
author: Sheryl Gay Stolberg

title: No. 2 Official at F.B.I. Is Said to Be Retiring Before End of Year
description: The departure of Christopher G. Raia, a veteran agent, comes a few months after another deputy left the F.B.I.
author: Devlin Barrett

title: Some Haitian Families Fleeing the U.S. for Canada Are Being Separated at the Border
description: Driven to Canada by deportation fears, some members of Haitian families are being denied entry, turned back and detained by U.S. authorities.
author: Miriam Jordan

title: Trump’s Extraordinary Nvidia Intervention Sidelines National Security Concerns
description: President Trump’s move to put Jensen Huang back at the helm of Nvidia caps his indifference to the warnings of his own intelligence agencies.
author: Peter Baker

title: Trump Toasted Floyd Mayweather, Who Owes the IRS, at Crypto Gala
description: At his third dinner for buyers of his memecoin digital tokens, the president’s honored guests included Floyd Mayweather, who owes the I.R.S.
author: Sharon LaFraniere

title: American vs. Chinese Mahjong: Why the Rivalry Is Stirring Controversy
description: American mahjong, with its own tiles and rules, has overshadowed the traditional Chinese game. The rivalry has fueled anger and cultural misunderstanding.
author: Amy Qin
